title: Vesper and the Vector
premise: Isandro Lockridge, a terraformer hauling cargo through contested orbits, has spent three years quietly tending a garden meant for colonists not yet born—until the colony's children begin sharing a single dream that points to his hidden past as a fleet signals officer who once faked the transmission that keeps two rival fleets from open war. As the children's dream spreads and a truce-expiry deadline approaches, Isandro must decide whether to keep the lie alive, confess it, or let the truth burn everything down. In the end he broadcasts the real record of what happened, sacrificing his anonymity and nearly his life, but the honesty forces both fleets to negotiate rather than fight—and the garden finally gets its people.
about_author: Mirabel Nakamura is a former hydroponics technician who writes science fiction aboard slow freighters between contracts. Her work explores how ordinary caretakers become unlikely heroes when systems fail.

chapters.title: The Garden Without Gardeners
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He tends the sealed biodome meant for future colonists, cataloging seedlings while cargo drones queue outside. Establishes his routine, his loneliness, and his careful habit of staying unremarkable in station records. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by guilt he won't name.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A routine haul takes him through the demilitarized corridor where Halcyon Fleet and Meridian Concord ships shadow each other. He witnesses a near-collision defused only by an automated handshake protocol. Emotional beat: unease—the truce feels thinner than anyone admits.

chapters.title: What the Children Saw
chapters.summary: Colony teacher Sefa's POV. Six children draw identical images: a tower of green light under two suns that don't exist. Sefa reports it; the colony council dismisses it as mass suggestion. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into institutional denial.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest Anomalies
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Station auditor Ryn Voss flags discrepancies in Isandro's supply requests—nutrients far exceeding the dome's logged capacity. Isandro deflects, but realizes someone is reading his files closely. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The dream now reaches forty children, each adding detail: a locked door, a voice counting down. Parents panic; the Concord garrison offers to 'help investigate.' Emotional beat: community fracturing along old fleet loyalties.

chapters.title: Signal Ghost
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He recognizes the countdown cadence from the dream—it matches the falsified distress loop he transmitted three years ago to trigger the truce. Someone or something is replaying it. Emotional beat: dread of being found.

chapters.title: Ryn's Offer
chapters.summary: Ryn Voss's POV. The auditor privately reveals she knows Isandro's biometrics don't match his identity chip. She doesn't report him—yet—because she suspects the truce itself is built on fraud and wants the truth. Emotional beat: wary alliance over shared secrets.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Deadline
chapters.summary: Halcyon Captain Oyelaran's POV. She receives orders to prepare for truce expiry in ninety days and is told the Concord's surrender broadcast was never verified. She begins pulling archived signals. Emotional beat: duty versus doubt.

chapters.title: The Dome at Night
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Following the dream's imagery, he finds a dormant relay node buried beneath the biodome—an old military transmitter still cycling fragments of his forged signal into the colony's water-recycling network, seeding the children's dreams via neural-resonant filtration. Emotional beat: horror at his own echo.

chapters.title: Sefa's Question
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She confronts Isandro after noticing his name appears in the dream's final detail—a door marked with his old service number. He lies badly. Emotional beat: the first crack in his invisibility.

chapters.title: Concord Interest
chapters.summary: Meridian agent Dae-Ho's POV. The Concord intercepts Oyelaran's archive queries and dispatches Dae-Ho to the colony to find whoever holds the original transmission logs. Emotional beat: cold professional menace closing in.

chapters.title: Silencing the Relay
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. With Ryn's help, Isandro shuts down the buried transmitter—but destroying evidence of the forgery would also destroy proof the truce was engineered to stop a massacre, not start one. Emotional beat: the lie's terrible double edge.

chapters.title: The Children Stop Sleeping
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Cut off mid-dream, the children wake screaming, sharing now a vision of fire instead of gardens. Colony doctors blame the shutdown. Riots spark between fleet-affiliated families. Emotional beat: guilt made communal.

chapters.title: Oyelaran Finds the Loop
chapters.summary: Oyelaran's POV. Her analysts trace the forged distress signal to a relay near the colony and identify its operator by service number: Lockridge, I., listed dead three years ago. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing the ghost is alive.

chapters.title: Dae-Ho Arrives
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Dae-Ho corners Isandro in the cargo bay, offering protection in exchange for the original logs—which would let the Concord claim the truce was Halcyon's fraud and justify first strike. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: What the Garden Was For
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Isandro's POV. Three years earlier: the real distress call came from a civilian convoy both fleets were about to destroy; Isandro faked a mutual-atrocity broadcast to force them apart, then erased himself. Emotional beat: understanding that the lie was mercy.

chapters.title: Truce Expires at Dawn
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Both fleets hold firing positions; the colony evacuates nonessential personnel; Ryn gives Isandro her shuttle codes. He chooses to broadcast the full authentic record—including the convoy's black box proving both sides fired first. Emotional beat: resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, climax part one. From the dome's transmitter he sends everything: the convoy deaths, his forgery, his confession. Both fleets' weapons lock on the colony. Emotional beat: terror and strange peace as he stops hiding.

chapters.title: Ceasefire, Broken Open
chapters.summary: Oyelaran and Dae-Ho's alternating POV, climax part two. Confronted with proof their own commands ordered the convoy strike, both captains refuse engagement and demand joint inquiry. Their superiors waver; the fleets stand down. Emotional beat: courage cascading upward.

chapters.title: Trial of the Gardener
chapters.summary: Ryn's POV. Isandro surrenders to a joint tribunal. The children testify that the dream showed them the truth they needed to ask for. Verdict: guilty of forgery, credited with preventing genocide—sentence commuted to supervised service. Emotional beat: justice without erasure.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The first colonist families arrive to claim the biodome. The children plant seeds alongside Isandro, no longer dreaming but remembering together. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, epilogue. At evening (vesper) light, he walks the rows with Ryn and Sefa, his name restored to the records. Two fleets share the orbit peacefully—for now. He plants a tree whose fruit he'll never taste. Emotional beat: survival's price paid gladly for a future he'll only glimpse.
